svg.title: How the screenshots renew themselves
svg.desc: After a change of main that touches a file of .github/screenshots-paths.txt, after every release and every week, the plan of the screenshot bot starts a run by hand, as the branch bot and a person do; without scripts/screenshots.sh, the bot renders nothing. The runs by hand render one at a time, the newest main. Each shard that .github/screenshots.toml names renders its pictures of that commit side by side, without secrets, and each picture whose pixels stayed the same keeps its committed file. When pixels changed, the job collect puts the shards together, and when main changed none of these files while they rendered, one pull request from bot/screenshots holds the new pictures, the files that the settings name and the width and height that the pages name for the pictures, and merges itself once every check passes; when main looks as rendered, the bot closes it. When main changed one of them meanwhile, as when the pull request before merged, or when the pull request conflicts with main later, the bot renders main anew: by itself, or started by the branch bot. So every picture shows the project as it is.
